messages:
anya (platform): proposal — SLA-aware throttling for plan mapping. idea: instead of rigid per-key hard caps for enterprise we give a best-effort burst pool that prioritizes by SLA tier and falls back to pro/free behavior when exhausted. thoughts?
kevin (sre): curious what "SLA-aware" buys us vs simpler soft/hard caps. is this complexity worth it? :thinking:
ram (platform): it lets us keep p99 latency SLOs for enterprise customers during noisy neighbors by routing their burst to reserved capacity first, then to shared with graceful throttling. avoids immediate 429s.
maria (product): customers keep asking for "no surprises" — enterprise wants predictable behavior under spikes. if we can guarantee degraded but non-fatal responses (e.g., queued or degraded model), that's huge for renewals.
anya (platform): right. proposal sketch: - free: strict soft cap with fast 429s and short cool-down - pro: higher soft caps + token-bucket burst smoothing, background retry hints - enterprise: reserved burst tokens + SLA routing; if reserved exhausted, we try degraded path (smaller model or longer tail) before 429.
kevin (sre): how do we measure/account for reserved burst? need telemetry per-org for burst usage, cost delta, and rollback hooks. also audit trail for billing.
ram (platform): agree. implementation idea: extend our quota service schema with fields: "sla_tier", "reserved_burst_tokens", "fallback_policy". sample config payload: ```json
{"plan":"enterprise","sla_tier":"gold","reserved_burst_tokens":100000,"fallback_policy":"degrade_then_429","per_minute_limit":50000}```
maria (product): can we surface that in console as "Burst remaining" and an alert when <20%? customers will want visibility.
anya (platform): yes — Console work: - show burst burn rate, last 24h peak, estimated runway - allow toggling fallback behavior per customer (degrade vs hard-throttle) - expose predicted cost impact if enterprise uses bursts regularly
kevin (sre): operational concerns: rollout plan must include kill-switches and defaults for when quota service lags. we shouldn't gate user requests on a single quota RPC. cache locally with short TTL and safe defaults.
ram (platform): implementation notes: - local cache w/ sliding window counters - central quota service as source-of-truth asynchronously reconciling - token accounting ledger for billing jobs to consume later
anya (platform): UX question: when we degrade, how does the API signal it? proposal: HTTP 200 with header `X-Redwood-Fallback: degraded-model` plus structured metadata in response. also emit usage event `quota.fallback` with reason.
maria (product): that makes sense. also add a console flag to disable automatic degrade for customers who prefer immediate 429s.
kevin (sre): A/B rollout suggestion: enable SLA-aware throttling for 10 enterprise orgs + synthetic load tests, then evaluate p99/p95 latency, error rates, and cost delta.
ram (platform): metrics to track: per-org p50/p95/p99 latency, 429s/sec, fallback.rate, reserved_burst_consumed, billing.adjustment. dashboards + alert thresholds.
anya (platform): quick prototype plan: 1) extend quota schema + DB migration 2) local cache layer + fallback header 3) console display + toggle 4) small canary on prod 5) expand. timeline ~3 sprints.
kevin (sre): add chaos tests: simulate quota-service latency and partition. ensure graceful fallback is safe.
maria (product): pricing note: if enterprise consumes reserved bursts often we should have an overuse billing rule or encourage larger reserved pool. need copy for sales and billing.
anya (platform): agree — docs + billing rule: auto-bill bursts above threshold at premium rate or convert to committed add-on.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: quota-service/feature/sla-burst -> staging at 2025-08-18T15:02:30Z
ram (platform): action items: @kevin to draft telemetry dashboard, @maria to write proposal for billing and console copy, @anya to PR schema change, I'll prototype local cache. can we sync tomorrow 10:30?
kevin (sre): I'll take dashboard. 10:30 works.
maria (product): I'll draft billing copy and sales FAQ.
anya (platform): PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/quota-service/pull/423 — basic schema + tests. feedback welcome.
kevin (sre): quick nit on PR: please add metrics tag for "fallback_reason" values to avoid sparse cardinality.
anya (platform): good catch, will add.
ram (platform): one more thing — include a feature flag to opt orgs into experiment group so we can A/B without deploy.
maria (product): thanks team. excited — if this works it's a great differentiator for enterprise reliability. :rocket:
anya (platform): cool — closing this thread, will follow up with PR link updates and canary plan.
